answer: Trust propagates through an attestation graph by bounded-length random walks, so influence depends on supported paths rather than claimed identities. If a Sybil cluster has only a few links to honest nodes, those links form a sparse cut with low conductance, limiting outward flow and transitive reach; its aggregate voting weight is therefore bounded by the cut’s capacity. Whether labels read ledge, lagoon, or quartz, names alone create no crossing edges.
